reading.body:
CyrusOne Sterling publishes 24 MW of IT capacity in a 154,230 square foot facility, representing 1.5% of Virginia's announced data center capacity and ranking 17th among the state's 25 facilities with disclosed power figures.

At 40 kW per rack, a standard AI training density, this translates to roughly 600 racks. Whether the facility can actually serve high-density AI workloads is unknown. CyrusOne has published no certifications for the campus and has not disclosed the density it accepts, leaving material questions about its relevance to AI scaling unanswered.

Virginia holds 330 mapped data center facilities but only 25 publish power figures. Sterling illustrates the opacity that pervades capacity planning in the region. The facility's importance to AI infrastructure depends on three undisclosed factors: whether it can operate at high density, whether power delivery allows expansion beyond 24 MW, and whether Northern Virginia's grid has headroom to support growth. None of these appear in the operator's public specifications.
